name: UPPAbaby Minu V3
price_note: UPPAbaby US list price; BabyGearLab lists $550, CR/Quartz $500

scores.cr_overall: Recommended; among CR's highest-rated lightweight strollers

specs.child_range: birth–50 lb, up to 40 in (carriage mode from birth)
specs.fold: 10 x 18 x 21.5 in (maker); BGL measured 3,497 cu in

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 (UPPAbaby recalls 21-158 RumbleSeat adapters and 22-215 Ridge jogger are other products)
why: Ranked first because three independent testers agree: BabyGearLab #1 of 12 (81, brakes 9/10), Consumer Reports recommended and among its highest-rated lightweight strollers, and Wirecutter's top pick; no recall of the Minu.
cautions: Heaviest of the top picks at 16.7 lb
Infant car seats need separate adapters (UPPAbaby Mesa/Aria, select Nuna, Cybex, Maxi-Cosi, Clek)
BGL's own spec table marks it not carry-on compatible despite UPPAbaby's IATA claim; check your airline

name: Joolz Aer2 (Aer²)
price_note: Joolz US base stroller; Aer2 with Nest to Seat $768; earlier Aer+ bundles from $553.98

specs.child_range: 0 months–50 lb (newborn use needs cot or car seat, sold separately)
specs.fold: 9.1 x 17.7 x 21.1 in (BGL measured); maker 17.3 x 20.8 x 9.2 in, 14.3 lb

recall_status: Stroller not recalled. Aer2 car seat adapters recalled June 18 2026 (CPSC 26-568, ~3,840 units, false-lock fall hazard, refund)
why: BabyGearLab #2 (78) with a 9/10 brake score tied for best, and the older Aer+ scored 84; Wirecutter's runner-up. Ranked below the Minu because its car seat adapters were recalled in 2026 and it has no CR rating found.
cautions: If you own Aer2 car seat adapters (product ID NL311, sold Jun 2025–May 2026), stop using them and get the refund
Lower flat-surface maneuverability in BGL testing (5.0)
BGL tested the Aer2; the 84 score is for the earlier Aer+

name: Nuna TRVL lx (and TRVL)
price_note: TRVL lx at Nuna US; original TRVL (the model BabyGearLab tested) is $575

specs.fold: 14.25 x 21 x 27 in (maker, TRVL lx); 14.6 lb excludes canopy and armbar (~2.4 lb)

why: BabyGearLab #3 (75) with the best maneuverability in the group (9.0) and brakes 8/10, and Consumer Reports recommends the TRVL lx; no recall. Ranked below the Aer2 on a lower lab score and a bulky fold.
cautions: Large when folded (BGL measured 6,301 cu in); plan to gate-check
Wirecutter found it very large folded with the belly bar and the closed canopy covers the handlebar
Only Nuna PIPA seats click in

name: Baby Jogger City Tour 2
price_note: List price for the City Tour 2 eco at babyjogger.com (sale $279.99); shown out of stock there on 2026-10-04

specs.child_range: birth (with Baby Jogger infant car seat) to 45 lb

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 (Baby Jogger's last stroller recalls were 2009–2012)
why: All three testers rate it well: BabyGearLab #6 (71, brakes 7/10), one of CR's highest-rated lightweight strollers, and Wirecutter's budget pick; no recall. Ranked below the TRVL on lower BGL scores.
cautions: Out of stock on babyjogger.com on 2026-10-04 (listed as final sale); check retailers
Newborn use only with a Baby Jogger infant seat and adapters

name: Bugaboo Butterfly 2 (now sold as Butterfly 2 Plus)
price_note: Butterfly 2 Plus at bugaboo.com US; CR tested the Butterfly 2 at $599

specs.fold: 17.6 x 9.6 x 21.8 in (maker); weight is CR's figure for Butterfly 2

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for Butterfly (Bugaboo Dragonfly seat recall 24-730 is a different stroller)
why: Consumer Reports recommends the Butterfly 2 and found it scored well in every test category; the first-generation Butterfly scored 81 at BabyGearLab. Ranked fifth because BabyGearLab has not tested the Butterfly 2 and Wirecutter tested it but did not pick it.
cautions: The Butterfly 2 Plus (lie-flat from birth) is newer than the tested Butterfly 2 and has no independent test yet
Wirecutter: footrest must be folded down by hand, buckle lets straps click in the wrong place
Car seats need adapters

name: gb Pockit+ All-City
price_note: Amazon price for Velvet Black on 2026-10-04 (other colors up to ~$265); gb has no US web store; BabyGearLab lists $330

specs.fold: 21.3 x 13 x 8 in (BGL measured, 2,215 cu in, smallest tested)

why: BabyGearLab #4 (73) and its Most Compact pick, with brakes 8/10 and the only stroller BGL rated carry-on compatible; no recall. Ranked sixth because Wirecutter dismissed it as not sturdy enough and its maneuverability is below average (5.5).
cautions: Not for babies under 6 months unless used with a compatible Cybex infant seat
Frame flex and small 5.1 in wheels; poor on grass, gravel and curbs
Retail price varies by color and seller

name: Inglesina Quid 3 (Quid³)
price_note: Inglesina US list price; on sale for $319.20 on 2026-10-04

specs.child_range: birth–55 lb per maker (BGL lists minimum 3 months)
specs.fold: 9.2 x 20 x 32 in (BGL measured); maker weight 14 lb

why: BabyGearLab #8 (64) with brakes 7/10; no recall. Ranked seventh because of the lowest harness score in the test (2.5: a third shoulder-height setting is advertised but missing) and Wirecutter found the harness hard to adjust.
cautions: Harness scored 2.5/10 at BabyGearLab; check the strap fit every ride
Self-stands only with a small kickstand (Wirecutter)
Car seats need the $49 Quid³ adapter

name: Summer by Ingenuity 3Dlite Convenience Stroller
price_note: summerinfant.com price; a 3Dlite+ variant was not found on the brand site, and the newer Ingenuity 3Dlite Jewel is $89.99 (untested)

specs.fold: 42.3 x 12 x 9.5 in (BGL measured, umbrella fold)

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 (Summer Infant's recalls in the window were non-stroller products)
why: Independently tested but last in BabyGearLab's group (55, brakes 6/10, lowest quality score); it ranks here only because it has a clean recall record and lab data, unlike the maker-claims-only models below it.
cautions: Double-action brake: both rear pedals must be set, which BabyGearLab warns parents may skip
Flimsy frame and plastic wheels (BGL); not for babies under 6 months
Wirecutter's old budget pick; no current Wirecutter or CR rating found

name: Stokke YOYO³ (6+)
price_note: Stokke US list price for YOYO³ from 6 months; on sale for $399.20 on 2026-10-04; newborn version listed separately
recall_status: Recalled Nov 14 2024 (CPSC 25-044): parking brake can disengage; ~2,890 units, serials starting 142AA below 0062239; refund
why: BabyGearLab ranks it 11th of 12 (56) with a weak 5/10 brake score and the hardest fold, Wirecutter found it frustrating, and its parking brake was recalled in 2024, so it sits below the 3Dlite despite a similar score.
cautions: Check the serial number against CPSC 25-044 (starts 142AA, below 0062239)
Two-hand fold that requires reaching under the seat (BGL ease of use 3.9)
CR has tested it but its rating was not visible
